label: echoed h (or i) fed back early in the copy phase of short (L=3-4) sequences
explanation: Very sparse feature (~167 activations in 1M sequences), active only in the copy phase at recall_idx 1-2 (t=4-6) of short sequences (L=3: 63% of mass, L=4: 36%). The input is almost always the model echoing back h (89% of mass) or i (11%), i.e. an early original token being fed back as the copy proceeds. Top activations are for L=3 sequences that start with h, at step L+1 (e.g. h i 0 <DEL> [h] i). The output token tends to be h, i or n. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, at first occurrences, or on longer sequences (L>=5). Magnitudes are small and fairly uniform (0.10-0.16); the highest ones are at L=3, recall_idx 1, with first token h. Precision is poor: most copy-phase steps where h is echoed in a short sequence do not fire, and I could not find a simple variable that separates them (the last original token and next_out did not help). So the description covers most of the activation mass, but it is not sufficient for the feature to fire.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: h, i, -, w, y, u; least: e, 3, z, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: h, i, n, u, d, 0; least: 1, k, b, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=4, L=3 & t=5.
